## What it catches

Bitsadmin started to create a download job, add a file to one, or set the command a job runs when it completes. Background Intelligent Transfer jobs survive reboots and run under the service, so intruders use them to download tools and to persist. Jobs created from PowerShell or the COM interface are not seen.

```yaml
selection_img:
- Image|endswith: \bitsadmin.exe
- OriginalFileName: bitsadmin.exe
selection_job:
  CommandLine|contains:
  - transfer
  - addfile
  - setnotifycmdline
condition: selection_img and selection_job
```

## Tested on

- fires: `one-line transfer job to the public profile`
- fires: `file added to an existing job`
- fires: `notification command set on a job for persistence`
- fires: `transfer job, event without a version resource`
- quiet: `listing the jobs of every user`
- quiet: `reading one job's state`
- quiet: `cancelling every job`
- quiet: `PowerShell listing BITS transfers`

## False positives

- Legacy software deployment or update scripts that still call bitsadmin to fetch packages

## What it does not see

- Jobs created with the Start-BitsTransfer cmdlet or through the BITS COM interface start no bitsadmin process
- A job created before logging began and only resumed later
- Process creation events recorded without the command line

## First checks

- List the jobs on the host with bitsadmin /list /allusers /verbose and read their notification commands
- Read the remote address and the local path of the job in the command line
- Check which account and parent process created the job
